NDT training in Memphis, TN: how it works for technicians and employers

Short answer: NDT training for Memphis is taken as self-paced theory online, with a Level III answering questions, followed by practical work in the Practical NDT simulator and hands-on at the employer's own facility. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Memphis. Your employer certifies you under its SNT-TC-1A written practice. We reply to every enquiry within one business day.

Memphis is a logistics city first. Freight moves through the airport, the rail yards and the river terminals every hour of the day, and the equipment that supports it, from aircraft structure to storage tanks to crane runways, gets inspected on a schedule. That is a different job market from a Gulf Coast refinery town or an aerospace corridor, and it changes what a new technician should learn first.

The employers here are mixed. A maintenance operation wants eddy current and penetrant skills on airframe parts. A terminal or refinery wants UT thickness gauging and magnetic particle work on weld repairs. A fabrication shop wants visual and MT examination on structural steel. One training path covers all of them, because the foundations of the methods are shared and the employer's written practice supplies the local detail.

This page explains the route from first lesson to certificate, which methods matter around the Mississippi River, how to judge schools and online options, and what an employer in the Mid-South should plan if it wants a crew qualified without sending people out of state. If you are already sure what you need, send us your methods, levels and head-count and we reply within one business day.

How to get NDT certified in Memphis: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

Most industrial employers in the Memphis area certify technicians under a written practice based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. The recommended practice describes what the employer should require, and the employer decides the final details. The sequence is the same whatever the method.

  1. Find or be hired by an employer with a written practice. A course on its own certifies nobody. If you are job hunting, put "working toward Level I" and the methods you have studied on your résumé; hiring supervisors in the region respond well to documented study.
  2. Complete the formal training hours. Your employer's written practice names the hours for each method and level. The training-requirements matrix lists the SNT-TC-1A recommended figures so you can see what a typical programme asks for.
  3. Log supervised experience. Hours on real work, signed by a certified technician, are the slowest part of the path. Start the log from your first day on a job.
  4. Pass the general examination on method principles and terminology.
  5. Pass the specific examination on the employer's own procedures, equipment and acceptance criteria.
  6. Pass the practical examination on representative specimens, scored by a Level III or an examiner working under one.
  7. Keep a current vision record. Near-vision acuity and colour-contrast checks are recorded at the interval the written practice sets. The SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker walks through the usual criteria.
  8. Receive certification from the employer, and recertify at the interval the written practice sets.

The alternative is ASNT central certification, where ASNT issues the credential after you pass its examinations. It suits individuals who do not have a sponsoring employer yet, and some customers prefer it. Atlantis NDT prepares candidates for both routes. The training FAQ covers common questions about how the two compare.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Memphis technicians

Courses follow the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge for each method. The table shows where each method turns up in the Memphis market, so you can choose in the order that gets you working fastest.

MethodWhat the course coversWhere it is used around Memphis
Visual testing (VT)Weld and fit-up inspection, lighting, gauges, record keepingStructural steel fabrication, tank and pipe repair, crane and rail equipment checks
Magnetic particle (MT)Magnetising techniques, field direction, indication interpretationWeld repairs on ferrous equipment, rail and truck components, lifting gear
Penetrant (PT)Process control, dwell times, interpretation on non-magnetic metalsAluminum and stainless parts in maintenance shops, cosmetic and structural welds
Ultrasonic (UT)Thickness gauging, straight-beam and angle-beam weld examinationRefinery and terminal piping, tank bottoms, plate and weld checks in steel work
Radiography (RT)Exposure technique, image quality, film and digital interpretationPipe welds, castings and pressure boundaries; requires separate state radiation training
Eddy current (ET)Impedance-plane interpretation, probe selection, calibrationHeat exchanger tubing at process plants and airframe surface inspection

Level I builds the core skill: performing calibrated examinations under supervision. Level II adds independent interpretation and evaluation against codes, which is why most employers treat it as the working grade. See the Level 1 NDT training and Level 2 NDT training pages for method-by-method detail. Level III is for people who write procedures, run the written practice and grade the examinations; ASNT Level III preparation is delivered the same self-paced way.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Memphis

Of the volumetric methods, UT is the one most Memphis employers use day to day. Thickness readings on pipe, vessel shells and tank floors feed corrosion tracking. Angle-beam examination of welds replaces radiography where the specification allows it and a site cannot clear an area for a radiation source.

A good UT course in this market covers sound-wave behaviour, transducer selection, calibration blocks, couplant, and how to separate geometric signals from real flaws. It also spends time on documentation, because an unrecorded reading cannot be audited. Our ultrasonic testing training page lists the modules, and the practice tests let you check your knowledge before the employer's general examination.

If you only learn one method before you apply for jobs, learn VT well and add UT thickness gauging next. VT is the entry point on nearly every inspection crew, and UT thickness is where entry-level technicians often get their first paid hours.

Where NDT technicians work around Memphis

Air freight maintenance. FedEx runs its largest hub at Memphis International Airport and maintains aircraft there. Aircraft maintenance uses penetrant, eddy current and visual examination on structure and engine parts, following the manufacturer's manuals and the operator's FAA-approved programme. Employers in that field write their own qualification requirements, so SNT-TC-1A-based foundations help but the programme is theirs.

Refining and terminals. The Valero refinery on the south side and the product and chemical terminals along the river operate pressure vessels, tanks and piping. Inspection there follows API standards for in-service equipment and ASME codes for repairs. Atlantis NDT does not teach API inspector certification, and some employers ask for it on top of NDT qualification.

Steel and fabrication. Nucor's Memphis mill and a long list of fabricators serving rail, barge and construction customers need weld inspection to AWS structural codes and to customer specifications. Some also require a certified weld inspector credential, which is a separate certification we do not provide.

Power and utilities. The Tennessee Valley Authority and the local utility operate generation and transmission assets in the region. Boiler and turbine outage work uses UT, MT and PT on pressure parts, and utility owners often impose contractor qualification rules of their own.

River, rail and bridges. Barge fleeting, rail intermodal yards and the Mississippi River crossings create steady structural inspection work. Bridge welding generally follows AWS D1.5.

Because the metro straddles three states, plenty of jobs are in Arkansas or Mississippi, a short drive from downtown. Certification issued by an employer is not state-specific, but radiation licensing is.

NDT schools and classes near Memphis: what to compare

Searches for "ndt school near me" and "ndt classes Memphis" turn up a mix of options: community-college programmes, private schools in other states with travel and lodging, vendor courses, and online providers. None is right for everyone. These are the questions that separate them.

  • Who certifies you at the end? Under SNT-TC-1A it is an employer. A school that issues a certificate of completion is giving you training documentation, which an employer may or may not accept toward its own requirements.
  • Where is the practical done, and on what? Practical skill comes from handling real specimens and equipment. Ask what hardware you will touch and how many hours.
  • Does the theory fit your shifts? A residential course means time off work and lodging. Self-paced theory fits around a job.
  • Which codes and methods does the content match? A course built around aerospace materials is a poor fit for pipe and plate work, and the reverse.
  • What do local employers accept? Call two or three Memphis-area employers and ask what documentation they want from new hires.

Atlantis NDT's approach is different from a brick-and-mortar school by design: online theory with Level III support, simulator rehearsal, and hands-on practice at an employer's facility under a written practice. That suits technicians who already have a sponsor and employers who want training that matches their own procedures. It does not replace a full-time school for someone who wants a classroom and instructor on site every day. See the training overview for the full catalogue.

Online NDT training in Tennessee

Theory can be learned online anywhere in Tennessee, and that is how most of our Memphis candidates start. Access opens the moment you enrol on the Atlantis portal. Modules are self-paced and a Level III answers questions as you go. Use Register & Buy Now when you are ready; the published US fees appear on this page, and the portal opens the course immediately.

Online learning covers the classroom portion of the SNT-TC-1A hours. It does not cover supervised experience or the practical examination, and no responsible provider will tell you it does. For regional context, see the Tennessee NDT training page, and for national information see NDT training in the USA. Nearby pages cover Nashville, Jackson and Little Rock.

Training a crew at your Memphis facility

An employer with a dozen technicians can run training and examinations at its own shop or terminal. The sequence looks like this.

  1. Review or write the written practice so it matches the methods and customer requirements you actually have. Our written practice development service handles that.
  2. Assign self-paced theory to the crew, scheduled around shifts and shutdowns.
  3. Run the practical examination at your site on your equipment and representative specimens, scored by a Level III.
  4. Build the specific examination around your procedures and acceptance criteria.
  5. Record everything in a format an auditor or customer can follow without help.

For a Memphis employer the usual drivers are a customer audit, a new contract that names a method, or turnover that has left the written practice stale. A Level III review before the audit is cheaper than a finding after it. Learn about outsourced Level III consulting if you have no certified Level III on staff. Ask about onsite training for a Memphis crew and tell us which codes your customers specify.

Radiography licensing in Tennessee

Radiography is regulated separately from certification. Tennessee is an NRC Agreement State, and the Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation's radiological health programme licenses radioactive material, including the sources used in industrial radiography. The licence belongs to the company, and radiographers have to meet the training and supervision requirements in the state rules and in the licence.

An RT course, including ours, teaches technique, image quality and interpretation. It does not license anyone to handle a source, and it does not replace the radiation safety training a licensee must provide. Most radiographers need both: the state-driven safety side and the SNT-TC-1A technique side.

Memphis crews often work across the river or the state line. Arkansas and Mississippi have their own radiation programmes, and reciprocity for out-of-state licensees follows each state's process, so check before mobilising a source.

Practise before your practical exam

Rehearsal shortens exam day. The Practical NDT simulator is a browser-based 3D environment where you can set up an examination, scan, and practise interpretation across method families and workplace settings, including a welding workshop and a storage tank site. It is a rehearsal aid, and it does not replace logged experience or the practical examination on real specimens at your employer's facility. For knowledge checks, the NDT practice tests offer method-by-method questions. Candidates who use both tend to arrive at the written examination with fewer surprises.

Training and examination support are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, an ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, with more than eleven years of international field experience.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Memphis

How long does it take to become an NDT technician in Memphis?

Theory can be finished in weeks if you study steadily. The longer part is documented experience, which your employer's written practice sets. Expect months to reach Level I working independence and a year or more to reach Level II.

Can I take NDT classes online and still work full time in Memphis?

Yes for theory. Self-paced modules fit around shift work. Practical examination happens in person at an employer's facility.

Which NDT method should I learn first?

Start with visual testing, then add magnetic particle or penetrant. Move to ultrasonic thickness gauging once you can document readings cleanly. Memphis employers hire for all of these.

Are there NDT jobs in Memphis for beginners?

Fabricators, maintenance shops and inspection contractors hire trainees, usually into VT or MT work first. Ask each employer how they sponsor Level I candidates. Pay varies by method, employer and shift, so ask each one directly.

Does my certificate transfer if I change employers?

Not automatically. A new employer starts by reading your records, then certifies you only under its own written practice. Keep copies of training, experience, examination and vision records.

What does NDT training in Memphis cost?

The published US fees are shown in the table on this page, and the portal opens your course at once. Employer groups and Level III support are quoted on request.

Is there an NDT school near me in Memphis that gives me a certification?

A school can give you training records. Certification under SNT-TC-1A comes from your employer, and ASNT central certification comes from ASNT. Check which one your target employers want.

Do I need a licence to do radiography in Tennessee?

The company needs a state licence for sources, and radiographers must meet the state's training requirements. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification.

Can you help us get ready for a customer audit?

Yes. We review written practices, training files and procedures through Level III consulting, and we can help build specific examinations around your procedures.

How do I start?
